title: Social Media Post Generator with Templates
description:
A Python tool that writes social media posts from a short brief about your business. The OpenAI model writes the parts of a post as structured output (hook, body, call to action, hashtags), and a Jinja2 template per platform assembles them in the right format.

  • Platforms: Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn and X, each with its own style hint, length limit and hashtag count.
  • Posts over the limit are regenerated with feedback (up to 3 attempts).
  • Hashtags are cleaned and de-duplicated; the model may only use facts from the brief.
  • Several variants per platform are spread over the next weekdays and saved as a CSV schedule for review.
prompts:
You write social media posts for a small business.
Platform: {platform} (style: {style}). The finished post must stay under {max_chars} characters.
Use only facts from the brief. Do not invent prices, dates, discounts or claims.
Return at most {max_hashtags} hashtags.

Input: the brief as JSON (business, business_type, audience, tone, post_type, details, link).
implementationSteps: Install the pinned dependencies and set OPENAI_API_KEY in .env.
Write a brief as JSON: business, audience, tone, post type, the facts to mention and an optional link.
Define the platforms with their length limit, hashtag count and style hint.
Create one Jinja2 template per platform that arranges hook, body, call to action, link and hashtags.
Ask the model for the post parts with responses.parse and a Pydantic schema.
Clean the hashtags, render the template and check the length; regenerate with feedback if it is too long.
Generate several unique variants per platform.
Spread the posts over the next weekdays at fixed times per platform and write posts.csv.
Review the CSV, then import it into your scheduling tool or post by hand.
performance:
Expectations, not measured results:

  • One model call per post, a few seconds each; a retry only when a post is too long.
  • Every post respects the configured length limit before it is saved.
  • Effects on reach or engagement are not known; compare variants in your platform analytics.
userExperience: You fill in a short brief and run one command. The tool prints the posts per platform with their planned date and character count and saves them to a CSV file. You edit or delete posts in the CSV and import the rest into your scheduling tool.
